faq.a: Tirzepatide has generally produced more weight loss and A1C reduction in comparisons, and SURPASS-CVOT showed cardiovascular safety, but it did not prove superiority on heart outcomes. The best choice depends on your health and coverage.
Most people regain appetite and much of the weight lost, and blood sugar can rise again.

name: GLP-1 and Incretin Therapies
blurb: Semaglutide, tirzepatide and the incretin drugs at the centre of modern type 2 care.
title: GLP-1 and Incretin Therapies
answer: GLP-1 receptor agonists such as semaglutide (Ozempic, Wegovy, Rybelsus) and the dual GIP and GLP-1 agonist tirzepatide (Mounjaro, Zepbound) lower blood sugar, reduce appetite and cause substantial weight loss. Large outcome trials now show heart protection with semaglutide, kidney protection in people with chronic kidney disease, and cardiovascular safety for tirzepatide.

explainer:
Incretins are gut hormones released after eating. GLP-1 tells the pancreas to release insulin when blood sugar is high, suppresses glucagon, slows stomach emptying and signals fullness to the brain. GIP is a second incretin with its own effect on insulin and fat metabolism. Drugs that mimic GLP-1, or both GLP-1 and GIP, therefore lower glucose with little risk of hypoglycemia on their own and reduce appetite enough to cause large weight loss.

The same molecules are sold under different brand names for different uses: semaglutide as Ozempic and Rybelsus for diabetes and Wegovy for weight, tirzepatide as Mounjaro for diabetes and Zepbound for weight. Common side effects are nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea and constipation, usually worst when the dose goes up. Less common but serious risks include gallbladder disease, pancreatitis and dehydration related kidney injury, and the labels carry a warning about a rare type of thyroid tumour seen in rodents. Stopping these drugs usually brings back appetite and weight, which is why many specialists now treat them as long term therapy.

developments.text: In SURPASS-CVOT, tirzepatide was noninferior to dulaglutide for major cardiovascular events in more than 13,000 people with type 2 diabetes and heart disease, 12.2 percent against 13.1 percent, a hazard ratio of 0.92.

sources.title: New England Journal of Medicine, SURPASS-CVOT

developments.text: In SOUL, oral semaglutide cut major cardiovascular events to 12.0 percent against 13.8 percent on placebo in about 9,650 high risk people with type 2 diabetes, a hazard ratio of 0.86.

sources.title: New England Journal of Medicine, SOUL

developments.text: The SUSTAIN-6 trial of semaglutide found more diabetic retinopathy complications, mainly in people whose A1C fell fast, which is why eye checks matter when starting these drugs.

sources.title: New England Journal of Medicine, SUSTAIN-6
